title: Compute exact canonical Clifford readouts for mixed width-13 observations
body:
At width 13, this gives exact Moore–Penrose coefficients for two families of mixed four-qubit observations.

- **A repeated input stabilizer with an arbitrary output tensor.** The complete linear representation uses 2,295 Lagrangians with sixteen complex features each. Its rank is exactly **36,720** over unrestricted output observations. For an entangled affine-quadratic output chart, the features can be produced by one parametric Gauss reduction per Lagrangian. The implementation then queries the requested coefficient. For every computational output string with a common input column, a four-bit quadratic form determines exactly which fibres survive the inverse. Exactly five global support sizes are attained.
- **Twelve repeated rank-one stabilizer sites and one arbitrary matrix.** The inverse reduces to 20 relative positions of Lagrangians with a marked vector, plus the five unmarked distance classes. The 256-dimensional singleton space has three distinct squared projection cosines, of multiplicities 1, 30 and 225. The calculation gives exact norms for superpositions and the sharp odd denominator 5,878,456,335,448,005,684,375 on its Gaussian-dyadic singleton coordinate operator.

One changed row already exhibits the mixing: its adjoint has 6,670,767,882,240 nonzero entries; after the canonical inverse, 8,338,459,852,800 are nonzero. An independent count of fixed flags recovers all 11 Gram eigenvalues of the 34,425-dimensional flag module, its forward and inverse traces, and a single-entry witness for the full flag inverse denominator.

The starting point is #7821's repeated-site decoder and #7816's central Gram. The proof credits the Clifford character data, the affine-quadratic contraction machinery and their original contributors. These are exact decoder and projection results at the existing selected exponent.

All 8 registered CPython 3.12 checks passed in the checkout and in a read-only, Git-free export of the submitted commit. The source-history, committed-byte, mode and export-inventory checks passed.
